newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 23.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- End of loyalist ceasefire feared after car-bombing in Belfast.
- Secret customs documents on an operation which led to the seizure of 13 tonnes of cannabis it Urlingford, Co Kilkenny, have been stolen and may be in criminal or IRA hands.
- The government is to appoint an ombudsman for children.
- The majority of Telecom Eireann's suppliers agree to new electronic payment system.
- Desmond group understood to have bought Barbados hotel. - Strong premiums growth at Lifetime.
- German purchase not without risk for Waterford Wedgwood. - Jefferson Smurfit appoints Mark Slevin as chief operating officer for the Nettingsdorfer Group in Austria.

- An Irish emigrant, who has been seriously ill in New York for 21 years, has been refused access to medical records which could prove his condition was caused by flea bites received shortly after his birth in a Dublin hospital.
- Death spiral feared after loyalists bomb car.
- Shoppers are on course to splurge 1.6 billion punts as the biggest shopping spree of the year reaches fever pitch.
- Dawn of Euro fails to light up Irish public interest.
- Pay pact puts Ireland at risk of breaking Euro entry rules.
- Creditors of ill-fated Evening News meet today.
